title: Mamluk armour triumph at Ain Jalut - the battle that stopped the Mongols
hook: Mamluk armour turned the tide at Ain Jalut, shattering the Mongol myth of invincibility.
description:

beats.say: In 1260, the Mamluks, once slave soldiers, surprised the world by crushing the Mongol advance at Ain Jalut.
While the Mongols boasted invincibility after sacking Baghdad, they underestimated the disciplined Egyptian cavalry's hidden tactics.
The Mamluk commander, Qutuz, lured the invaders onto the open plain of Al-Rashid, where dust choked their horses.
beats.visual: plain of Al Rashid desert landscape

beats.say: He ordered a feigned retreat, drawing the Mongol vanguard into a narrow gorge flanked by desert cliffs.
At the signal, hidden Mamluk archers unleashed a rain of arrows, shredding Mongol shields and morale.
The Mongol leader, Kitbuqa, fell under a crushing horse, his death turning the battle into chaos.
Meanwhile, Sultan Baibars arrived with reinforcements, his heavy cavalry smashing the remaining Mongol ranks.
The victory halted Mongol expansion into Africa, preserving Egypt's cultural renaissance and the Islamic world's stability.
Historians once claimed the Mongols simply fled, but recent scholarship shows they were outmaneuvered by superior strategy.
That day, the Mamluk steel and discipline rewrote the map of medieval power forever.
